why_how.text: Permanent pavement markings identify road centers, lanes, edges and special lane uses.
Yellow pavement lines separate opposing directions of traffic.
Yellow lines mark the center of two-lane roads and the left edge of divided highways, one-way streets and ramps.
Solid white pavement lines separate same-direction lanes and also mark a roadway's right edge.
As a general rule, broken traffic lines may be crossed and solid lines may not, except when making a turn.
A single broken yellow centerline on a two-way, two-lane road permits passing from either side only when conditions are safe.
Passing across a broken yellow centerline uses the lane for oncoming traffic.
A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing in either direction even without a NO PASSING sign.
With one solid and one broken yellow centerline, passing is allowed from the broken-line side only when conditions are safe.
With one solid and one broken yellow centerline, the driver on the solid-line side may not pass.
A shared center turn lane bordered by solid outer and broken inner yellow lines is reserved for left turns from either direction and cannot be used for passing.
On an undivided multilane road, broken white lane lines may be crossed to pass when the passing lane is clear.
On an undivided multilane road, a double yellow centerline cannot be crossed for passing and opposing traffic lies beyond it.
On the usual divided limited-access highway pattern, solid white marks the right edge and solid yellow marks the left edge of each roadway.
Broken white lines between same-direction lanes on a divided limited-access highway may be crossed.
Pavement words and arrows supplement regulatory and warning signs.
STOP AHEAD pavement wording announces a stop-sign intersection ahead.
YIELD wording or white triangles across a lane indicate that the driver must yield to approaching traffic.
SCHOOL pavement wording warns of a school zone ahead.
R X R pavement lettering marks an approaching railroad crossing.
BIKE LANE pavement wording identifies a lane reserved for bicyclists.
ONLY combined with a left or right pavement arrow reserves the lane for that turn.
Large white pavement arrows indicate travel direction on one-way roads and highway exit ramps.
